content: Combination therapy plays a critical role in the management of type 2 diabetes due to the progressive nature of the disease. Achieving and maintaining long-term glycemic control often necessitates the gradual addition of medications in a stepwise manner. Typically, initial treatment begins with metformin as the first-line therapy. However, as the disease advances and glycemic control targets are no longer achieved with monotherapy, additional pharmacological agents are introduced to sustain therapeutic effectiveness.
